clue.text: Overcharge for woollen coat

blocks.note: first meaning: to swindle someone by charging too much
second meaning: the woolly covering of a sheep

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests paying too much for a coat; in fact the verb and the noun are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip off a customer is to take their wool, as it were, and a sheep's shorn wool covering shares the same name.

clue.text: Trump rings dodgy chum unduly often

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and out of order, so the letters it describes are rearranged

blocks.note: in British slang to trump is to break wind
two rings, each the shape of the letter O
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A certain politician keeps telephoning a shady friend far more than is proper.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump looks like the politician, but it is the British schoolyard verb for passing wind; the capital letter is pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something excessively or more than is reasonable is doing it beyond the proper amount, an idiomatic adverbial phrase.

clue.text: Hurries up king entering original Cinque Ports at last

indicators.note: original can mean novel or newly made, so the letters are formed into a fresh arrangement
to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within another
only the final letter of the word it follows is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A monarch arrives at the historic Cinque Ports and everyone speeds up for the royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are a historic group of English Channel harbour towns; 'original' reads as describing them but signals a rearrangement of CINQUE into QUICEN, with K slotted in.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate or make faster is to speed things along, a standard synonym in the transitive verb sense.

clue.text: Grapple with story about lead characters in Citizen Kane

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another
the leading characters of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: a tale is a story
the opening letter of each word of the film title

explanation.surface: Getting to grips with the plot of the famous Orson Welles film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead characters' sounds like the stars of the film, but means the initial letters of its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a problem or opponent directly is to deal with it head-on, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Unflagging elders regularly engaged in mysterious rites

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
to be engaged in something is to be involved inside it, so one piece sits within another
something mysterious is puzzling and obscure, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tribal elders throw themselves energetically into secret ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of elders gives LES, which sits inside TIRES, a rearrangement of rites.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who never flags or grows weary keeps going with unflagging energy, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Is able to get one's drug

blocks.note: to be able to do something is that you can
to nab is to grab or get hold of
one is I, plus the 's

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they can obtain their usual supply of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read literally: I for one, followed by the S of the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant-derived substance, also called marijuana or hemp, is a widely used narcotic, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Legendary UFO lab rocked America

indicators.note: something rocked is shaken about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A mythical alien research facility shook up the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The UFO lab conjures Roswell, but its six letters are just raw material; the definition takes 'fabulous' in its older sense of belonging to fable.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a story of legend, so anything mythical or storied can be described with this adjective in its original sense.

clue.text: Boy in spectacles is on electronic instrument

indicators.note: one item sits inside another
in a down answer, sitting on something means placed above it, so one part follows the other

blocks.note: B is a standard abbreviation for boy
a pair of glasses looks like two letter Os
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A bespectacled lad plays a synthesiser.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an electronic instrument, but the instrument is a woodwind; electronic merely supplies E.
explanation.definitionFit: This double-reed woodwind is a member of the orchestra, so it is one example of the broader category.

clue.text: Badger home to locate aunt's last letter

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

blocks.note: to set something is to place or situate it
the final letter of aunt

explanation.surface: Someone needs the final letter from an aunt to find where a badger lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' could be a verb meaning pester, but here it describes the animal whose burrow is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The underground burrow system dug by these black-and-white mammals has its own special name in English.

clue.text: Latest thing is going round northern Sweden's mountains

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: the latest craze is all the rage
N is the abbreviation for northern
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A new trend is touring the mountains of northern Sweden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latest thing' reads as a news item, but it is a craze, which is a RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of connected peaks are called chains or ranges, so the plural noun names groups of mountains.

clue.text: Be very obvious criticism's not allowed

blocks.note: taking stick is receiving criticism
out means forbidden or ruled out

explanation.surface: A demand to be conspicuous, as nobody is permitted to criticise.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick is informal British for harsh criticism, as in 'giving someone stick'; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stands out or is conspicuous protrudes visibly, a phrasal-verb idiom for being plainly noticeable.

clue.text: I'll organise getting holiday book containing sex

indicators.note: to contain is to hold inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: leave is time off work
a tome is a large book
IT is an old euphemism for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to arrange things after picking up a racy holiday read.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex comes from the 1920s 'It girl' sense of sex appeal, a long-standing crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to hand a task over to you is offering to handle it yourself, an idiomatic spoken equivalent.

clue.text: The Queen's brought in to sleep in space for 36

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so one piece goes within another
one item is placed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
R for Regina, Latin for queen
an en is a printer's unit of space
to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: Her Majesty arrives to nap in a room meant for three dozen people.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is'; an en is a printing measure half the width of an em.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve is a dozen, so a trio of them makes this number, an arithmetic equivalence rather than a synonym.

clue.text: Herb comes from source of Tagus River in part of Spain

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so the first letter is taken
one item is placed inside another

blocks.note: the opening letter of the river's name
Aragon is a region of north-eastern Spain
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A herb is said to grow at the headwaters of the Tagus, in a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tagus really does rise in the Aragon area, which makes the geography look literal; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic plant with a liquorice flavour is used in French cooking, an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Inclination to look after nurse with cold, back on duty

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

blocks.note: to tend is to care for
EN is an enrolled nurse
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone wants to care for a nurse who has a cold and has returned to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back on duty' suggests a nurse returning to work; it only picks out the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning or propensity towards some behaviour is a natural disposition, a standard noun synonym.

clue.text: Cook gently put in white fish

indicators.note: something put in is inserted, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to simmer is to cook just below boiling
W is the abbreviation for white

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: poach some white fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White fish' reads as a food item, but white supplies W and fish alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish is a creature that moves through water, so it is described cryptically by what it does.

clue.text: Raised problem with copper getting fat, almost brawny

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising something turns it upwards so it reads bottom to top
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
lard less its last letter

explanation.surface: A policeman developing a weight problem, though still fairly beefy.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman, but it is the metal with symbol Cu; lard is the fat that loses its D.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly built, beefy person has well-developed muscles, so the two adjectives are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Hog the limelight in high society time after time

indicators.note: one thing coming after another means it is placed behind it in sequence

blocks.note: up means high
S is the abbreviation for society
T is the abbreviation for time
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A socialite repeatedly steals the spotlight among the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High society' and 'time after time' look like fixed phrases, but each word works separately: high, society, then one time following another.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw attention away from others is to outshine them, originally by moving upstage so other actors must turn their backs.

clue.text: Travel extensively taking our planet by storm

blocks.note: to seethe is to rage or storm
the world is the planet we live on

explanation.surface: Globetrotting and taking the planet by storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking by storm' is a stock phrase, but here storm is a verb meaning rage, and 'taking' merely joins it to the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeying widely across many countries is a common idiom for broad travel and gaining experience abroad.

clue.text: Came in first, guarding each president with gun

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround and protect it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to come first is to win
EA is the abbreviation for each
P is the abbreviation for president

explanation.surface: An election winner who protects each president while armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came in first' suggests winning a race; it is simply the past tense of win.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is one kind of arm used in combat, so it is an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Note has wrong tense in wording

blocks.note: te is a note in sol-fa
an X marks something as wrong
T is the abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A written note uses the wrong verb tense somewhere in its phrasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a grammar complaint; each word supplies a short piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The actual words of a document are its written content, so these nouns are near synonyms.

clue.text: Jack's quietly hiding keys in utility vehicle

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: J is jack in a pack of cards
p is the musical marking piano, quietly
E is a musical key, so two keys

explanation.surface: Jack quietly stashes the keys inside his four-by-four.
explanation.walkthrough: Keys suggests car keys, but here they are musical keys, two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: This rugged four-wheel-drive car was designed for general military use, and its name is a brand for an all-terrain vehicle.

clue.text: Will administrator's former partner finally settle court action?

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word
putting letters into action sets them moving, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
the last letter of the word
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Will the lawyer handling an estate let an ex-spouse settle the lawsuit at last?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court action' reads as a lawsuit, but action is the signal to rearrange court; 'Will' is the legal document, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named to carry out the instructions in a testament and distribute the estate holds this legal role.

clue.text: Chinese dynasty's spirit and civilisation ultimately endure

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter is used

blocks.note: the Han dynasty ruled China for four centuries
go is energy or spirit
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: The resilient spirit and culture of an ancient Chinese dynasty lived on.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit tempts as an alcoholic drink such as GIN, but it is GO, meaning energy or verve.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going and persist through difficulty is to hold out, a phrasal verb meaning to last or persevere.

clue.text: Thanks father with parting drink

indicators.note: a piece that parts another splits it open by sitting inside it

blocks.note: ta is British informal for thanks
pater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for father
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Saying thanks to Dad over a farewell drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parting drink' suggests a final round before leaving, but parting is the instruction to split PATER with W.
explanation.definitionFit: Water drawn from the mains supply is something you consume as a beverage, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Disheartened, buy into spreading largesse

indicators.note: to lose heart is to lose the middle, so the central letter is removed
spreading things out scatters them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the phrase with its central I taken out

explanation.surface: Someone demoralised still signs up to a scheme of distributing generous gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Disheartened seems to describe a person, but it removes the middle letter of the seven-letter phrase 'buy into'.
explanation.definitionFit: Generosity in giving, or the gifts themselves, is a synonym for liberal giving or a generous reward.
